docs.title: DPG Compliance Checklist — Health Without Borders (Frontend / Flutter client)
docs.text:
Health Without Borders ships as two repositories — a FastAPI backend and this Flutter client — that are assessed against the Digital Public Goods Standard separately, because several indicators land on one side only (e.g. the API is what exposes non-PII data; the client is what encrypts data at rest on the device). This checklist scores each of the nine indicators as they apply to this repository specifically; where the underlying mechanism actually lives in the backend, the note says so and points there instead of this repo claiming credit for work it doesn't do.

  • Status legend: ✅ Met · 🟡 Partial · 🔴 Gap
# DPG Standard indicator Status What this repo actually does 1 Relevance to the SDGs (SDG 3 — Health) ✅ Met This is the field tool brigades use: NFC-based patient registration, offline consultations/vaccines, and guardian consent capture for migrant and pediatric populations. 2 Use of an approved open license ✅ Met MIT (LICENSE), independent of the backend's own licensing. 3 Clear ownership ✅ Met PROJECT_CHARTER.md names guane emerging technologies as owner and lays out the trademark policy for "Health Without Borders" / "HWB" separately from the code license. 4 Platform independence ✅ Met One Flutter codebase ships to iOS, Android, macOS, Linux, Windows and Web (pubspec.yaml, per-platform runners in the repo). SQLite FFI is initialized for Linux and Windows (sqflite_common_ffi), while native SQLite is used on mobile/macOS and IndexedDB on Web. The only hard platform dependency is NFC hardware itself, which is inherent to the feature, not a vendor lock-in — the web build falls back to a no-op NFC stub (nfc_service_stub.dart) rather than failing. 5 Documentation ✅ Met MkDocs site (mkdocs.yml) covers local setup, project structure, offline-sync design, and the domain-model contract with the backend — published from docs/. 6 Mechanism for extracting non-PII data 🟡 Partial The actual extraction mechanism (the aggregated stats API) lives in the backend repo, not here. This repo only surfaces it: StatsRepository calls it and the brigade-metrics screen renders it. Marked Partial rather than Met because this repository, on its own, doesn't expose the data — it depends on the backend being deployed and reachable. 7 Adherence to privacy & applicable laws ✅ Met Guardian consent is captured and stored per Ley 1581/2012 (GuardianConsent, signature capture); Android's data_extraction_rules.xml explicitly excludes app data from cloud backup and device-transfer, and on iOS/macOS the local database lives in Application Support/hwb_db flagged NSURLIsExcludedFromBackup while its AES key is stored with first_unlock_this_device (ThisDeviceOnly), so PHI never leaves the device outside the app's own sync path. 8 Adherence to standards & best practices ✅ Met patient_record.dart mirrors the backend's FHIR R4 / RDA schemas field-for-field so the two repos can't silently drift; flutter analyze + flutter test + coverage gate every PR (ci.yml; branch protection and merge gating for develop/main defined declaratively in .github/rulesets/protect-develop-main.json). 9a Do No Harm — Data Privacy & Security ✅ Met This is where the client carries the most weight: local SQLite is AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest (LocalDatabase), with its key kept device-only in the keychain/keystore and the file excluded from iCloud/computer backups on Apple platforms, NFC device/card payloads are separately AES-256-GCM encrypted using an authenticated key ring (NfcKeyring / NfcPayloadCodec), auth tokens sit in OS-level secure storage, UI is gated by role (UserRole), and any guardian-absent "emergency access" view is logged locally and synced for audit (logEmergencyAccess). 9b Do No Harm — Inappropriate & Illegal Content 🟡 Partial There's no open posting surface — the only free-text is clinician-entered clinical notes (optionally via speech-to-text). Still open: a one-line statement in the docs saying this explicitly, so it's not just implicit from reading the code. 9c Do No Harm — Protection from Harassment ✅ Met Same CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and enforcement contact as the backend; this repo has no separate community space, so nothing extra to moderate here.

docs.title: What the app does
docs.text:
Health Without Borders stores a patient's clinical record on the patient's NFC device (a chip the patient carries; a minor's guardian carries a second one) and keeps a synchronized copy on the server. Because brigades often work without a stable internet connection, the app is offline-first: you can register patients and record care with no signal, and the app will synchronize automatically when a connection is available.

A single patient has one shared record across all participating organizations, so any authenticated professional can read and update it at the point of care.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A mobile device with NFC enabled (Android) and the app installed.
  • Your login credentials, provided by your organization administrator.
  • Patient NFC devices and, when applicable, guardian cards.

Note: The interface is available in Spanish and English. You can switch the language at any time from the header (see Getting Started).

docs.title: How this guide is organized
docs.text:
1. Getting Started — Log in, understand the home screen, switch language, and sign out safely.
  2. Registering a New Patient — Create a patient, assign the device, and add guardians.
  3. Finding & Viewing a Patient — Search, scan a device, and read the clinical history.
  4. Consultations & Vaccines — Add care to a patient's record.
  5. Syncing Pending Records — Understand and clear the sync queue.
  6. Statistics — Review brigade activity (administrators).
  7. Administration — Manage users and organizations (administrators).

docs.text: These screens are for administrators. They let you manage the people and organizations that use the platform.

docs.title: 1. Manage users
docs.text:
Open Manage users to see the users in your organization, grouped by role (for example, Administrator, Doctor, Nurse).

From a user's detail you can:

  • Create a new user.
  • Deactivate a user — the account is suspended but not removed.
  • Reset the password of a doctor or nurse (a superadmin can also reset an organization administrator's). The app shows a temporary password once: give it to the user, who must replace it when they sign in. All of the user's sessions end.
  • Delete a user — the account is removed.

docs.title: 2. Manage organizations
docs.text:
Open Organizations to see the list of organizations. Selecting one opens its details (identifier, status, number of users, number of patients).

From an organization's detail you can:

  • Deactivate the organization.
  • Delete the organization.

Note: Deleting an organization protects patient records — patient data is never removed. Associated user accounts are deactivated together with the organization.

docs.title: 3. A note on roles
docs.text: What you can see and do depends on your role. Organization administrators act within their own organization; super administrators can act across organizations. If an option is not visible to you, your role does not include that permission.

docs.title: Consultations & Vaccines
docs.text: This page explains how to add clinical care — consultations and vaccines — to a patient's record.

docs.title: 1. Add a consultation
docs.text:
1. Open the patient's record (by scanning the device or searching), or use the summary screen right after registration.
  2. Tap Add consultation.
  3. Complete the consultation details and save.

docs.title: 2. Add a vaccine
docs.text:
1. From the same summary or record screen, tap Add vaccine.
  2. Enter the vaccine information and save.

docs.title: 3. How the device is updated
docs.text:
When you add a consultation or a vaccine, the device is marked as modified so the new information is written back to the NFC chip and synchronized to the server. If you are offline, the change is stored locally and appears in the pending-to-sync queue until a connection is available.

Note: After adding care, use Finish to complete the encounter. Remember to write the device if it is still marked as pending.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page covers logging in, the home screen, changing the language, and signing out safely.

docs.title: 1. Logging in
docs.text:
1. Open the app. On the login screen, enter the email and password provided by your organization administrator.
  2. Tap Log in.

Your access depends on your role (for example, medical staff, or an organization administrator). Administrators see additional options such as Statistics, Manage users, and Organizations.

If an administrator created your account or reset your password, the app asks you to choose your own password before anything else: at least 12 characters, not a common one. You can change it later from Change password on the home screen. Changing it signs you out on every other device.

After several wrong passwords the account is paused for a while; the app tells you how long to wait.

Note: Once you are logged in, the app keeps your session active as you move between screens. If your session expires, you will be asked to sign in again — any records you registered in the field are kept on the device until they can be synchronized.

docs.title: 2. The home screen
docs.text:
From the home screen you can reach the main actions:

  • New patient — register a patient and assign a device.
  • Search patients — find an existing patient.
  • Pending to sync — review records waiting to be uploaded. A gold badge shows the number of records still stored locally (including any duplicates or errors).

Administrators also see Statistics, Manage users, and Organizations.

docs.title: 3. Changing the language
docs.text:
The app is bilingual. Use the ES / EN switch in the header to change the language instantly — titles, buttons, filters, and cards update immediately, with no need to restart the screen. Dates are also shown in the format that matches the selected language.

The language switch is available on the main screens, including New patient, Search patients, Pending to sync, Manage users, and Organizations.

docs.title: Finding & Viewing a Patient
docs.text: This page explains how to find an existing patient and how to read a patient's clinical record from their device.

docs.title: 1. Search for a patient
docs.text:
1. From the home screen, tap Search patients.
  2. Enter the patient's identifying details (for example, document number or name).
  3. Tap Search.

If no match is found, the app shows the message: "No patient found with these details. Please check the fields." Review the values you entered and try again.

docs.title: 2. Read a patient by scanning the device
docs.text:
At the point of care, the fastest way to open a record is to scan the patient's device:

  1. Choose the read option and tap Start.
  2. Hold the patient's device (or the guardian card) against the back of the phone.
  3. The patient's record opens once the device is read.

Note: The device identifier is unambiguous, so scanning always opens the correct patient. Manual search is best when the device is unavailable.

Guardian device of another minor: offline, the record opens from the guardian device only if that device holds this patient's record. If it holds another minor's record (or one from before the patient device was reassigned), the app shows only the data on the patient device, read-only, and says so. Online, the server always returns the right record.

Retired devices: a patient or guardian device that was retired (lost, damaged or replaced) shows "This device was retired and no longer belongs to HWB." and does not open the record, online or offline. Offline, the phone checks a list of retired devices that it downloads each time it syncs with a connection. If it has never synced, the record opens with a warning that the device could not be checked.

docs.title: 3. Read the clinical record
docs.text:
When a record is open, the information is organized into tabs:

  • Summary — the patient's key information at a glance.
  • Consultations — the list of recorded consultations.
  • Vaccines — the vaccines registered for the patient.
  • Consultation details — the full detail of a selected consultation.

Dates are shown in the format that matches the selected language (ES / EN).

docs.title: 4. Emergency access
docs.text: In urgent situations, the app provides an emergency ("break-glass") access path so that care is never blocked. Every emergency access is recorded in an audit log (who accessed the record and when). Use it only when clinically necessary.

docs.title: 5. Reassign a device
docs.text:
When a patient device or a guardian device is lost or damaged, go to Loss of device, open the patient's record and tap Reassign device to write a new, blank device in its place. The old device stops working online, and offline once this phone knows about it: right away on the phone that made the reassignment, and on other phones after their next sync with a connection.

The patient's other devices still name the old one: the patient device lists the guardian devices, and each guardian device holds the patient device and both guardian devices. After the reassignment the app asks to update the other devices:

  • Write now — write them right away, in the same visit.
  • Later — the record shows "NFC backup out of date" until you write them.

Write them before the patient leaves. If a guardian device was reassigned, until the patient device is written the new guardian device does not open the record offline, and the old one still does.

docs.title: Registering a New Patient
docs.text: This page explains how to create a new patient, assign the patient's NFC device, and add one or two guardians.

docs.title: 1. Start a new registration
docs.text:
1. From the home screen, tap New patient.
  2. The registration form opens. You can switch the language (ES / EN) at any time from the header.

docs.title: 2. Enter the patient's information
docs.text:
Complete the fields in each section:

  • Patient NFC device — the identifier of the device you will assign (you can also scan it in the next step).
  • Identification — document type, document number, first and last names (second name and second surname are optional).
  • Demographic data — date of birth and biological sex.
  • Nationality — choose from the list. If the nationality is not listed, select "Other".

Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*). The Continue button advances through the steps.

docs.title: 3. Assign the patient device
docs.text:
When prompted, the app shows the guided writing screen ("Patient device"):

  1. Tap Start.
  2. Hold the patient's device against the back of the phone until the app confirms the write.

Note: You can tap Skip to finish the registration without writing the device immediately. In that case the patient is saved locally and marked as "Pending to write to the NFC device", so you can write the device later.

docs.title: 4. Add guardians
docs.text:
For patients who require a guardian, you can register up to two guardians:

  1. Enter each guardian's information.
  2. Capture the guardian's consent signature when requested.
  3. When prompted with the "Guardian card" screen, hold the guardian card against the phone to write it.

Note: The guardian's consent signature is preserved on the server; it is not lost when the guardian card is synchronized.

One guardian device per minor. A guardian device holds the record of one patient, and offline it opens that record. A guardian with two or more children needs a separate guardian device for each child. If the device you scan already belongs to another patient, the app says "This device already belongs to another patient. Each minor needs their own guardian device: use a blank one." and does not use it.

docs.title: 5. Finish and save
docs.text:
On the summary screen you can:

  • Add consultation or Add vaccine (see Consultations & Vaccines).
  • Tap Finish to complete the registration.

The patient is saved locally first and appears in the pending-to-sync queue until the app uploads it to the server.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text: The Statistics screen gives administrators an overview of brigade activity — patients, vaccines, and nationalities. Availability depends on your role.

docs.title: 1. Access and scope
docs.text:
• Organization administrators see the statistics for their own organization.
  • Super administrators can see all organizations, or narrow the view to a single one using the organization dropdown.

You can switch the language (ES / EN) from the header.

docs.title: 2. Filter by period
docs.text:
Use the quick filter buttons to choose the time window:

  • All — all available data.
  • This month — the current month to date.
  • Last 20 days — a rolling recent window.
  • Custom — opens a calendar where you select a specific date range.

The figures and trends update to match the selected period, comparing it against the previous one where applicable.

docs.title: Syncing Pending Records
docs.text: Because the app is offline-first, records you create in the field are first saved on the device and then uploaded to the server. This page explains how to review and clear those pending records.

docs.title: 1. Why records are pending
docs.text: When there is no connection — or when a device still needs to be written — new patients and updates are stored locally and queued for synchronization. The home screen shows a gold badge with the number of records still pending (including any duplicates or records with errors).

docs.title: 2. The sync queue
docs.text:
Open Pending to sync from the home screen. Each record is shown as a card with a clear status:

  • Pending — waiting to be uploaded.
  • Error — the upload did not complete; the card explains, in plain language, what to do.
  • Duplicate — the record matches one already on the server.

docs.title: 3. Synchronize
docs.text:
• Tap Sync now on a single record, or Sync all to upload the whole queue.
  • Tap Review to inspect a record before syncing.

When a record uploads successfully, it leaves the queue and the home badge count goes down.

docs.title: 4. Notices: changes the server did not apply
docs.text:
Sometimes the server accepts an upload but keeps its own version of part of the record — for example when another device updated the patient first, or when the copy came from a patient or guardian device that was already replaced. The rest of the record is saved. The queue then shows a notice for that patient that says what was not applied, and the home screen counts it next to the pending records.

Scan the patient device again to see the server's version, then update the patient device and the guardian device from the profile. Tap Got it to dismiss the notice. The same notice appears on the patient's profile.

docs.title: 5. Records left by another user
docs.text:
Records stay on the phone when their author signs out. If someone else signs in on the same phone, they do not see those records and cannot sync them: the queue only says how many are waiting. They sync when their author signs in on that phone again. Nothing is deleted when users change.

Note: Technical system-error details are intentionally hidden from this screen to keep it clear. When you sign out, the app warns you if records are still pending — sync them first whenever possible so nothing is left only on the device.
